newsitem.title: INDIA: India court says phone taps violate privacy right.
newsitem.headline: India court says phone taps violate privacy right.

text.p: India's Supreme Court on Wednesday ruled that telephone taps by the government violated a fundamental right to privacy, the Press Trust of India reported.

"Telephone tapping is a serious invasion of an individual's right to privacy," PTI quoted two judges of the country's highest court as saying in their decision on a case filed by a civil rights group.
The judges also called for the government to set guidelines regulating telephone taps.

"It is necessary to lay down procedural safeguards for the exercising of government's powers relating to phone tapping so that a person's right to privacy is protected," PTI said, quoting the judges' decision.
It said the judges had ruled that taps violated fundamental rights, including the right to privacy, under the India Telegraph Act of 1885, which regulates Indian telecommunications.
Until new guidelines were fixed, the court ruled that phone taps be authorised by senior officials in the federal home (interior) ministry, or their counterparts in different states.
